faq.title: Still have questions?
faq.q1.question: Is the app free?
faq.q1.answer: Yes — there's no billing system of any kind in the app.
faq.qOpenSource.question: Is Aura Player open source?
faq.qOpenSource.answer: It will be — the plan is to publish the full source code, no hidden parts. The repository link will appear here as soon as it's published.
faq.q2.question: Which systems are supported?
faq.q2.answer: Today, only Windows 10/11 (64-bit). Using native Windows APIs to embed video in the app window currently rules out other platforms.
faq.q3.question: What is DLNA?
faq.q3.answer: A standard that lets devices on the same local network — TVs, NAS, phones, PCs — discover each other and stream media between them, no internet required.
faq.q4.question: Do I need internet?
faq.q4.answer: No, for local or DLNA playback — it all happens on your network. Internet is only needed for playing externally-hosted live streams (Live HLS).
faq.q5.question: How do I connect my TV?
faq.q5.answer: If your TV (or an app like BubbleUPnP on your phone) supports DLNA, turn on "Receive" mode in Aura Player's Settings — your PC will show up as a "Cast to device" option.
faq.q6.question: Where can I download it?
faq.q6.answer: From the download section above, as soon as the first public release is published.
faq.q7.question: Why does Windows show a warning when installing?
faq.q7.answer: The installer doesn't have a digital signature (a paid certificate) yet, so Windows SmartScreen warns as a precaution — normal for independent apps. Click "More info" → "Run anyway".

downloadPage.title: Download Aura Player
downloadPage.subtitle: Before installing, two quick things worth knowing: what you're agreeing to, and why Windows might warn you the first time you run it.
download.certificate.title: What's that Windows warning about?
download.certificate.intro: If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC" when you open the installer, that doesn't mean Aura Player has a virus. Here's the real reason:
download.certificate.whatIsIt.title: What is a code-signing certificate?
download.certificate.whatIsIt.body: It's a digital seal, issued by a certificate authority and paid for by the developer, that "signs" the installer — proving to Windows who published it and that the file hasn't been tampered with since it was built. Large software companies pay for this every year.
download.certificate.whyMissing.title: Why doesn't Aura Player have one (yet)?
download.certificate.whyMissing.body: A code-signing certificate costs a few hundred dollars a year from reputable providers. As a free, independent project, that cost doesn't make sense yet — the plan is to sign the installer once the project has enough revenue or support to justify it.
download.certificate.smartscreen.title: So what is SmartScreen actually doing?
download.certificate.smartscreen.body: Windows SmartScreen works on reputation: files signed by known publishers, or downloaded many times by other users, pass through without a prompt. A brand-new, unsigned installer that hasn't been downloaded much yet — like Aura Player's — triggers the warning as a precaution, even though it's safe.
download.certificate.notVirus: This isn't an antivirus result. No antivirus engine scanned the file and found anything malicious — it's just Windows being cautious about a new publisher.
download.certificate.step1Hint: Shown as small text inside the warning window.
download.certificate.step2Hint: This button only appears after step 1.

1. About the software
Aura Player is free software, provided "as is", without warranties of any kind, express or implied. By installing and using the app, you agree to these terms.

2. License to use
You may install and use Aura Player freely, for personal or commercial purposes, on as many computers as you like. The project is expected to become open source — once that happens, the source code license terms will be published alongside the repository.

3. No warranties
The developer does not guarantee the software will be error-free or run without interruption. Use is at your own risk. Under no circumstances will the developer be liable for direct or indirect damages arising from use of the app.

4. Content you play
Aura Player is a media player — it does not host, distribute, or take any responsibility for the content you choose to open, whether a local file, a DLNA server on your network, or a live stream. You are solely responsible for having the rights to whatever you play.

5. Privacy
Aura Player does not collect, store, or send personal data to external servers. The only network connection made by the app itself (outside of playback) is an optional update check against GitHub, which can be turned off in Settings. "Receive" mode (DLNA) only opens ports on your local network, to let your own devices send media to the PC.

6. Third-party component (mpv)
Aura Player uses the mpv player (free software, under its own license) internally to play video. It's already bundled with the installer — there's nothing to download or install separately.

7. Changes
These terms may be updated in future versions of the app or site. The version in effect is always the one published on this page.

support.title: Fix common problems
support.subtitle: Causes and fixes for the most frequently reported Aura Player issues, organized by category.
support.categoryDlna: DLNA and casting to the PC
support.stillNeedHelp.title: Didn't find your issue?
support.stillNeedHelp.body: Open an issue on the project's repository describing what happened — the more detail (what you did, what you expected, what actually happened), the faster it gets fixed.
support.i1.question: The app won't open, or closes itself right away
support.i1.answer: In most cases, your antivirus removed or quarantined an internal installer file (common with new software that doesn't have a reputation yet — see the code-signing section above). Check your antivirus quarantine and restore Aura Player, or add an exception before installing. If it keeps happening, reinstall on top of the current installation.
support.i2.question: "Windows protected your PC" when trying to install
support.i2.answer: Expected for an installer that doesn't have a paid digital signature yet. Click "More info" and then "Run anyway". See the full explanation (what the certificate is, why this happens) on the Download page.
support.i3.question: "Could not connect to mpv"
support.i3.answer: Aura Player uses mpv (bundled with the installer itself) to play video. This message shows up when that bundled file can't be found — almost always because an antivirus removed or quarantined that part of the app. Check your antivirus quarantine and reinstall Aura Player.
support.p1.question: The screen stays black, but audio plays normally
support.p1.answer: Video is rendered in a native window embedded inside the app window — in rare cases (outdated GPU drivers, or switching apps with Alt+Tab) that window can fail to redraw correctly. Try switching to another app and back; if it persists, update your video driver or restart Aura Player.
support.p2.question: I changed the playback speed, but it doesn't seem to have any effect
support.p2.answer: This was a known bug in earlier versions, now fixed: the speed did change for real, but the on-screen indicator didn't keep up and snapped back to showing "1x". Update to the latest version.
support.p3.question: Subtitles or audio open in the wrong language
support.p3.answer: Aura Player automatically prioritizes Portuguese tracks (pt-BR, pt, por) when available in the file. If the content has no Portuguese track, it falls back to the file's default track. You can switch manually from the Audio and Subtitle menus in the control bar.
support.l1.question: The live stream stalls frequently
support.l1.answer: Aura Player continuously measures your connection's real quality and adjusts its buffer on its own — the less stable the network, the bigger the safety margin it keeps. Frequent stalling usually means your internet is currently below the stream's bitrate; in Settings → Live, the "Stable" profile prioritizes not stalling over low latency.
support.l2.question: The live stream starts noticeably behind the real "live" point
support.l2.answer: A small initial delay is expected (the app needs to measure your connection before deciding how close to "live" is safe to get). If the initial delay seems too large, in Settings → Live you can switch the buffer profile to "Low latency" or set a custom target latency.
support.l3.question: What do the "Excellent", "Good" and "Unstable" labels mean?
support.l3.answer: It's a real-time health reading of your connection, combining network margin, stability, and recent stall history — not just how much buffer is built up. "Good" can show up even with a healthy buffer, if your internet has little headroom over the stream's bitrate.
support.d1.question: The PC doesn't show up as a "Cast to device" option
support.d1.answer: "Receive" mode needs to be turned on in Aura Player's Settings, and Windows Firewall usually asks for permission the first time — you need to allow access on private networks. Check both before trying to cast from your phone again.
support.d2.question: The app can't find any DLNA server on the network
support.d2.answer: The PC and the server (TV, NAS, another phone) need to be on the same Wi-Fi network. Some routers have a setting called "client isolation"/"AP isolation" that stops devices from seeing each other even on the same network — if the search finds nothing, it's worth checking that setting on the router.
support.d3.question: DLNA receiving stops working after switching networks/Wi-Fi
support.d3.answer: If "Auto-reconnect" is turned on in Settings → DLNA, Aura Player detects the network change on its own and restarts receiving. Without it enabled, you'll need to manually turn "Receive" mode off and back on after switching networks.
